A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TA-TiTok/MaskGen research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original tokenizer reconstruction experiments, MaskGen generation results, component ablations and appendix evaluations on COCO and ImageNet.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction and generation experiments and adds latent attention/code-swapping analyses and a revised component ablation.

M1.justification: The principal tokenizer architecture, losses and MaskGen variants are retained. However, Section 4.2 deletes v1's timestep embedding from the description of adaLN conditioning, while v1 Figure 3 already depicts text/aesthetic conditioning. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a correction to the description.

E1.justification: Training retains DataComp, CC12M, the LAION subsets, JourneyDB and DALLE3-1M. Evaluation retains ImageNet reconstruction/class-conditional generation and text-to-image generation on MJHQ-30K, GenEval and COCO. The added latent-swapping examples are representation diagnostics, without established new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 6 introduces TiTok-based KL MaskGen-L controls alongside TA-TiTok, with and without aesthetic conditioning, in the downstream generation ablation. Comparator membership in the main MJHQ-30K, GenEval, COCO and ImageNet/MAR comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The 64-token VQ aesthetic-conditioning experiment in v1 Table 12 is replaced by a KL MaskGen-L experiment crossing tokenizer choice with aesthetic conditioning in v2 Table 6. v2 also introduces final-encoder-layer attention and latent-code replacement diagnostics. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and reported training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism analysis through attention maps and code-swapping experiments testing local semantic specialization and global style control (Section 5.2, Figures 4 and 8). Its factorial tokenizer/aesthetic ablation also directly tests the contributions to generation quality. Existing text-guidance-type/place and token-count ablations remain available despite relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests for these experiments. The new analyses introduce no uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Under the same reported DataComp-to-ImageNet setting, Table 3 changes TA-TiTok VQ rFID for 32/64/128 tokens from 4.09/2.68/1.78 to 3.95/2.43/1.53; corresponding IS values also increase. New KL-control scores and latent-swapping outcomes are reported, while the VQ no-aesthetic result (FID 8.66, GenEval 0.49) disappears. The principal MJHQ-30K, GenEval, COCO and MAR results remain unchanged; the differently configured aesthetic ablations are not direct performance improvements.

T1.justification: v2 numbers and rewrites the existing tokenization equations using explicit ignored outputs and different concatenation notation. These express operations already described in v1; no substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: one-stage text-aware 1D tokenization, discrete/continuous representations, and efficient open-data MaskGen generation competitive with existing models. The new supporting analyses do not redefine these principal claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets latent attention and swapping as evidence that tokens specialize in semantic regions or global style, and argues that dynamic allocation explains efficient encoding. It also concludes that text-aware tokenization contributes more than aesthetic conditioning. The existing resolution, convergence and model-scaling limitations are retained in Appendix I.

D1.justification: v2 Figure 3 explicitly documents separate modality projections and feedforward networks, and Section 3 adds the continuous-token random-masking detail. Its conclusion now reports released code and weights, although future-release wording remains in the abstract/introduction. Existing training hyperparameters and filtering/recaptioning instructions are retained, largely through relocation.

R1.justification: v2 adds six introductory references, including FlowTok, FlowAR, Beyond Next-Token and 1.58-bit FLUX. The related-work arguments and novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged. Renumbering and the publication update for Randomized Autoregressive Visual Generation do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: Experimental prose is condensed and reorganized around tokenizer and generator results. Training details and the text-guidance-type ablation move into the appendix, limitations move to Appendix I, and references precede a separately headed supplement. Most abstract, introduction, related-work and method prose is retained, making this a targeted reorganization.

P2.justification: The central TA-TiTok and MaskGen diagrams are substantially redrawn, Figure 1's image selection changes, and new attention/code-swapping Figures 4 and 8 are added. The aesthetic ablation is expanded and moved into the main text, while v1's duplicate VQ/KL summary table is removed. These substantially revise the visual presentation beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2's crossed tokenizer/aesthetic ablation provides more direct evidence for component effectiveness, while latent-swapping examples and detailed architecture diagrams improve interpretability and clarity. These are useful but limited gains: headline benchmark evidence and limitations remain stable, the earlier VQ aesthetic test is replaced, and the updated reconstruction scores are not explained. Overall, the supporting evidence and exposition improve modestly.
